modelNotes: Minutes Engine 1.1 uses player-pool status plus season, last 5, and last 10 minutes from NBA history.
Unknown starters retain their historical minutes baseline and are not treated as confirmed bench players.
Missing injury information does not mean a player is cleared; publication eligibility requires confirmed game status and role.
Roles are Core Starter, Starter, Rotation, Bench, Deep Bench, and Inactive.
No odds or betting lines are used.

injury.shortComment: Horford (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks, but will play Thursday against the Grizzlies, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: Horford will miss the first half of a back-to-back set Wednesday due to a back injury, but will be available Thursday. Charles Bassey could see an expanded role in Horford's absence, while Horford could see a larger role than usual Thursday with Draymond Green set to rest.

injury.shortComment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injury.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injury.detail: Williams sustained a left hamstring strain in the Nov. 9 win over New Orleans, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Boston. LJ Cryer will likely continue seeing increased burn in Williams' stead.

injury.shortComment: Harper (hip) won't play in Thursday's game against the Clippers, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
injury.detail: Harper took a hard fall late in Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons. He will now miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign, with his next opportunity to play coming Saturday against the Pelicans. There should be an update on Harper's condition in the next day or two. In the meantime, Julian Champagnie is in line to start.

injury.shortComment: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
injury.detail: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

injury.shortComment: Stewart (illness) won't play Wednesday against the Cavs.
injury.detail: This will be Stewart's second straight game on the sidelines, which should lead to more minutes for Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post. Stewart's next chance to play will come Thursday against the Warriors.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
injury.detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

injury.detail: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

injury.detail: Williams will take the night off Thursday after appearing in Portland's last five contests. He will presumably be back on the floor Saturday against the Knicks. In the meantime, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen should see more minutes behind Donovan Clingan.

injury.detail: Rollins wasn't included on the initial injury report, though he's since been ruled out for a second straight game due to an illness. His next chance to play will come Thursday versus Portland. With the 24-year-old combo guard sidelined, Kasparas Jakucionis and Gary Trent will likely continue seeing increased minutes.

injury.detail: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

injury.shortComment: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

injury.detail: This will be Jerome's third straight game on the inactive list due to the hip injury, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Thursday's meeting with the Warriors. Cam Spencer should continue to start in his absence and Javon Small will have the chance for some extended minutes. Cedric Coward should continue to see some increased playmaking responsibilities with Jerome sidelined.

injury.detail: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

injury.shortComment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
injury.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

injury.shortComment: Ingram (heel/Achilles) will remain on the inactive list for Thursday's game in San Antonio.
injury.detail: Ingram was cleared for full-contact work on Nov. 6, and he's been playing 5-on-5 for the past couple of weeks. Head coach Tyronn Lue said before Sunday's 113-105 win over the Hornets that he was hopeful Ingram would make his Clippers debut during their upcoming four-game road trip, so while he'll remain on the sidelines for Thursday's game, it sounds like there's a chance he could play Saturday in Dallas.

injury.shortComment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

injury.shortComment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injury.detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injury.shortComment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

injury.shortComment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injury.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

injury.shortComment: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
injury.detail: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

injury.shortComment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

injury.shortComment: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

injury.shortComment: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
injury.detail: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.
